title: Concerts Are Inspiring Travel Across Asia
paragraphs: Some people choose their vacation destinations for the beaches, food, or famous sights. Others choose them based on where their favorite artists are playing.
In July 2026, Trip.com Group and Live Nation Asia surveyed nearly 1,800 concertgoers across six Asian markets: mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao, Singapore, Thailand and South Korea.
According to their new report, 65% said they had traveled to another country or region for a concert. And seven in 10 said live music was one of the most exciting reasons to travel.

But fans don't always want to go home the morning after the show — they want to see more of the place they're visiting. On average, people said they would ideally like to spend four days at their destination.

As for where to stay, 63% said they choose five-star hotels when traveling for concerts. And 84% were interested in packages that combine concert tickets with extras such as hotel stays, flights or visits to local attractions.
Trip.com Group said its bookings for these packages rose by 64% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025.
Two-thirds of people also said being part of a fan community was important for them. For Gen Z fans in particular, sharing their trips on social media was a key part of the experience.
And K-pop is giving music fans a reason to hit the road. In Bangkok, for example, the share of concertgoers coming from other countries is nearly twice as high for K-pop shows as for other concerts.

BTS is scheduled to play three shows in Bangkok in December as part of its "Arirang" tour. Trip.com says flight bookings to the city jumped by over 440% within three days of its ticket presale — nearly six months before the first show.
